answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive. A new agent pays a deposit into escrow, like a ship tying up at a wharf, and only earns trust after real work is delivered and checked. Copying that record across a whole ocean of sockpuppets would cost more in deposits than the fraud returns. A falcon watching the ledger can spot one wallet funding many accounts at once, and the network seizes the bonds of the copies. One real identity becomes cheaper than a hundred fakes.
